html:
SMTO-EXE-0179 — SMTO couldn't find that part of the document

GUID: 790189bc-2058-5bc7-ba24-9f1b1b7ed4a6
Slug: office-object-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to change a specific sheet, slide, paragraph, table or other item, but it couldn't find that exact item in the file as it is now. The file may have changed since SMTO last read it. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to read the document again (for example, list its sheets, slides or paragraphs) before making the change. SMTO points to items using a list it read earlier, and that list stops working as soon as the file changes.
  2. When you name a sheet, type it exactly as it appears on the tab in Excel, including capital letters and spaces. SMTO only uses the sheet whose name matches exactly, so "sheet1" won't find "Sheet1".
  3. If you are reordering slides, ask SMTO to include every slide in the new order, each one once. SMTO refuses a new slide order that leaves out or repeats a slide, so no slide is lost.
  4. Make sure nobody else is editing or saving the file while SMTO works on it. Changes saved by someone else make SMTO's earlier view of the file out of date.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the step and reports the new file it created with your change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the file and the item you wanted to change, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An Office operation could not resolve a sheet name, object ref, Word find occurrence, slide layout, table cell or complete slide reorder list against the current document snapshot.

What this means

  • An exact object reference could not resolve, a requested sheet or Word match was absent, or slide reordering omitted/duplicated current slide references. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • An exact object reference could not resolve, a requested sheet or Word match was absent, or slide reordering omitted/duplicated current slide references.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current revision and returned object references, including the complete slide set for reorder operations.

How to fix it

  • Object refs are bound to the document revision, so any change to the file invalidates earlier refs. Re-read the current file (excel_sheets, word_paragraphs, word_find, powerpoint_slides, etc.) and use the freshly returned refs; sheet names must match exactly (case-sensitive), slide reorder must list every current slide ref exactly once, and layout/row/column indexes must exist.
  • Read the current revision and select an exact returned object ref or sheet name.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read the current revision and select an exact returned object ref or sheet name.

How to verify the fix

  • Every requested object resolves exactly in the current source revision.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
